title: Isolate weight decoding and create lightweight prefetch proxy
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: Model start-up time and memory spikes for large models are driven by synchronous decode+dequant paths inside the model loader. The current loader mixes format parsing, weight decoding, and tokenizer handshake which couples slow filesystem/IO and CPU-bound decode with latency-sensitive runtime initialization. This makes cold-starts brittle and complicates incremental upgrades of serialization libraries.

Goal: Move heavy-weight decode/transform work out of the hot path by implementing a lightweight prefetch proxy ("decode-as-a-service") that can run co-located with the runtime or as a shared sidecar. The proxy will be responsible for: decoding/transforming weights from on-disk shard formats (including new quant formats), producing mmapped-ready artifacts, and exposing a small HTTP/gRPC API for the runtime to request activation. At the same time, separate tokenizer initialization into a deterministic handshake that does not block weight activation.

Scope of work:
- Extract weight decoding pipeline into an independent binary (prefetch-proxy) with pluggable format adapters.
- Introduce a memory-mapped artifact format (lightweight header + contiguous decoded slab) for fast memory mapping in the runtime.
- Add eviction and residency policy hooks: LRU-based eviction tuned by sequence-length distribution and model priority.
- Upgrade HF serialization dep from 2.3.x to 3.0.1 in the proxy only; runtime will remain pinned until we validate ABI compatibility.
- Keep on-disk shard manifests and weight index backward-compatible (adapter layer).
- Add a simple RPC contract between runtime and proxy (activate, prefetch, stat, release).
- Ensure tokenizer handshake remains unchanged for tokenization contract; decouple tokenizer init so runtime can start serving metadata endpoints before all shards activated.

Why unique: Rather than a single monolithic loader refactor, this ticket introduces a separate process boundary to reduce blast radius, enable independent upgrades (dependencies, quant libraries), and create a reusable prefetch service for multiple runtimes (hosted/dedicated/private).
acceptance_criteria: Cold-start p95 for 2B-parameter model reduced by >=10% on benchmark infra compared to baseline
Memory spike during activation reduced by >=20% on our standard 32GB GPU host
Proxy binary can decode existing shard formats and the new mmapped artifact format is loadable by runtime without extra deserialization
No change to tokenizer public API; tokenizer handshake can complete independently of shard activation
Automated e2e tests (unit + integration) covering prefetch->activate->release flow in CI
Clear migration path documented for Dedicated and Private deployments
implementation_notes: Build proxy in Rust for safe zero-copy mmapping and compatibility with existing runtime FFI
Use a small adapter interface for format handlers so we can add custom quant formats without modifying core proxy binary
Proxy exposes gRPC control plane and local Unix socket for low-latency deployments; HTTP fallback for Private air-gapped installs
Write a runtime shim (C++) that will negotiate: existing manifest -> proxy activation token -> mmapped file descriptor handoff
Keep runtime read path unchanged by designing mmapped artifact header to mimic current in-memory layout
Instrument proxy with Prometheus metrics: decode_time_seconds, active_artifacts, resident_bytes, eviction_count
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Prototype proxy and runtime shim in a feature branch; validate on dev-models with CI perf harness
Phase 1: Roll out to internal canary infra for a subset of small/medium models (2B-8B) with monitoring dashboards
Phase 2: Opt-in Beta for dedicated customers; provide migration docs and optional dual-loader config
Phase 3: Default routing for hosted where proxy is enabled; provide rollback path to legacy loader via feature flag
Gate: Must hit acceptance criteria metrics and complete a security review before Phase 2
risks: Increased operational complexity: new process to monitor and upgrade
Compatibility: mmapped artifact layout must be resilient to runtime ABI changes
Security: proxy runs with access to weights; must enforce KMS/HSM integration and RBAC for Private installs
Performance regression: bad eviction policy could cause thrash and actually increase p95 under bursty workloads
performance_metrics: Decode.cpu_seconds_per_gb: track and regress if >10% increase
Eviction.rate_per_hour: track and keep <5 for steady state workloads
tests: Unit: format adapter tests using synthetic shards
Integration: proxy + runtime shim with sample 7B model in CI using ephemeral VM
Stress: repeated prefetch/activate/release loops with randomized eviction parameters
Upgrade test: HF serialization 2.3 -> 3.0 decode compatibility test using archived checkpoints
Security: KMS access simulation in Private deployment image
